topic_ko: 실버 애로우리드는 영양의 배설물을 닮은 씨앗으로 쇠똥구리를 속여 씨앗을 퍼뜨림

passage: Plants have developed all sorts of clever tricks to move their seeds away from the parent.
A South African plant called silver arrow-reed relies on one of the strangest of them.
Its seeds are dark brown, rounded, and just over a centimeter across.
Both the way they look and the way they smell closely match the droppings of antelopes.
Dung beetles, which normally roll animal droppings underground to feed on them or lay eggs in them, are fooled at once.
Within minutes of a seed hitting the ground, a beetle arrives and carefully rolls it away.
Only after burying it does the insect discover that the prize is neither food nor a nursery.
The beetle gives up and leaves, and the plant ends up with its seed safely planted underground.
choices: the feeding and breeding habits that make dung beetles useful to farmers
the chemical process that gives antelope droppings their strong smell
a plant that spreads its seeds by fooling dung beetles into burying them
the competition among South African plants for limited underground space
the damage that insects cause to the seeds of wild African plants
theme.explanation_ko: 배설물을 닮은 씨앗으로 쇠똥구리를 속여 씨앗을 묻게 만드는 식물의 번식 방식이 글 전체의 초점이므로 ③이 주제이다.
theme.distractor_ko: ① 쇠똥구리의 습성은 속임수가 통하는 이유로만 쓰인 배경이다. ② 배설물의 화학적 성분은 언급이 없다. ④ 식물 간 경쟁은 다루지 않는다. ⑤ 곤충이 씨앗을 해친다는 내용과 오히려 반대이다.

passage: Among the many ways plants scatter their seeds, one South African species stands out.
The silver arrow-reed produces round, dark brown seeds a little bigger than a centimeter.
In appearance and in scent, these seeds are almost indistinguishable from antelope droppings.
Dung beetles by instinct roll such droppings underground to eat them or to raise their young.
So a beetle reaches a fallen seed in a matter of minutes and treats it exactly like real dung.
Once the seed is buried, the puzzled beetle finds it can neither eat it nor lay eggs in it.
It abandons the useless ball and goes off in search of genuine droppings.
The deceived insect has, without knowing it, done the work of planting the seed.
choices: 쇠똥구리는 배설물의 냄새로 먹이를 정확히 구별해 낸다.
식물의 씨앗은 크기가 클수록 멀리 퍼져 나갈 확률이 높다.
남아프리카의 곤충들은 서로 협력하여 토양을 비옥하게 만든다.
실버 애로우리드는 쇠똥구리를 속여 자기 씨앗을 대신 심게 만든다.
동물의 배설물은 식물이 자라는 데 가장 중요한 양분원이다.
gist.explanation_ko: 속아 넘어간 쇠똥구리가 자기도 모르게 씨앗을 묻어 주어 결국 식물이 이득을 본다는 것이 요지이므로 ④이 적절하다.
gist.distractor_ko: ① 쇠똥구리는 오히려 냄새에 속는다. ② 씨앗 크기와 확산 거리의 관계는 언급이 없다. ③ 곤충들의 협력은 나오지 않는다. ⑤ 배설물의 양분 역할은 이 글의 논점이 아니다.

passage: Nature is full of inventive solutions to the problem of moving seeds away from the parent plant.
The silver arrow-reed of South Africa may have the most cunning solution of all.
Its round, dark brown seeds are barely more than a centimeter wide.
To a dung beetle, they look and smell exactly like the droppings of an antelope.
Beetles therefore hurry to a fallen seed and roll it away with great care, just as they would real dung.
They bury it, expecting a meal or a safe place for their eggs, and find neither.
Disappointed, they leave the buried ball behind and hunt for the real thing.
Each failed beetle leaves behind a seed that has been planted for free.
choices: The Antelope: An Unlikely Gardener of Africa
How Dung Beetles Keep African Soil Healthy
Why Seeds Must Be Buried to Survive Drought
The Sharp Senses That Insects Rely On
Seeds in Disguise: Fooling the Dung Beetle
title.explanation_ko: 배설물로 위장한 씨앗이 쇠똥구리를 속인다는 내용이므로 ⑤이 제목으로 가장 적절하다.
title.distractor_ko: ① 씨앗을 옮기는 것은 영양이 아니라 쇠똥구리이다. ② 토양 건강은 언급이 없다. ③ 가뭄 생존은 다루지 않는다. ④ 곤충의 예리한 감각은 오히려 속아 넘어가는 것과 어긋난다.

passage: The silver arrow-reed of South Africa scatters its seeds in a most unusual way.
Its seeds are dark brown, round, and a little over a centimeter in size.
In both look and smell they are almost identical to antelope droppings.
Dung beetles normally roll such droppings underground to eat them or lay their eggs inside.
So a beetle reaches a newly fallen seed within minutes and rolls it away with care.
They have no choice but to abort and search for real dung balls.
The seed, however, has already been carried off and buried in the soil.
In this way the plant gets its seeds planted without lifting a finger.
implication.underlined: They have no choice but to abort and search for real dung balls.
choices: The beetles are forced to give up on the seed and look for genuine dung instead.
The beetles decide to share the seed with other insects nearby.
The beetles dig the seed up again and carry it back to the plant.

implication.distractor_ko: ② 다른 곤충과의 공유는 언급이 없다. ③ 씨앗을 다시 파낸다는 서술은 없고 오히려 묻힌 채 남는다. ④ 번식 중단은 본문에 없다. ⑤ 미리 구별하게 되었다는 학습 내용은 없다.

passage: Of the many methods that plants use to scatter seeds, the silver arrow-reed has a remarkably strange one.
Its seeds, which are dark brown and round, measure slightly more than one centimeter.
What makes them dangerous to beetles is how closely they resemble antelope droppings in look and smell.
When a seed drops to the ground, a dung beetle approaching it within minutes rolls it away as if it was antelope dung.
Beetles are often spotted rolling seeds that look and smell like real dung balls.
Only after burying the ball do they realize that they can neither eat it nor lay eggs in it.
Having no choice, the confused insects abandon the seed and look for genuine dung.
By tricking the beetles into burying its seeds, the plant plants them far more effectively.

The trick lies in the seeds themselves, which are dark brown, round, and just over a centimeter wide.

passage: The silver arrow-reed of South Africa scatters its seeds in a highly unusual manner.
Its seeds are dark brown, round, and slightly larger than a centimeter across.
Both their appearance and their smell are very close to those of antelope droppings.
Dung beetles instinctively roll such droppings underground to eat them or lay eggs in them.
Within minutes of a seed falling, a beetle rolls it away as if it were real dung.
After burying it, the insect finds that the ball is neither food nor a nursery.
It abandons the ball and goes off to look for genuine droppings.
The seed, meanwhile, is left planted in the soil exactly where the plant needs it.
summary.summary_template: Because the seeds of the silver arrow-reed closely __(A)__ antelope dung, deceived beetles __(B)__ them underground, and the plant is thereby planted without any effort of its own.
summary.explanation_ko: 씨앗이 영양의 배설물과 '닮아서'(resemble) 속은 쇠똥구리가 그것을 땅에 '묻어 주므로'(bury) resemble–bury 가 적절하다.
summary.distractor_ko: repel(밀어내다)·outgrow(자라서 벗어나다)는 씨앗이 배설물과 비슷하다는 서술과 반대이고, destroy(파괴하다)·collect(모으다)는 씨앗을 땅에 묻어 심어 주는 결과와 맞지 않는다.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 그러고 나서 쇠똥구리는 마치 그것이 영양의 배설물인 것처럼 씨앗을 조심스럽게 굴려 간다.
writing.answer: They carefully roll the seed away as if it were antelope dung.
writing.explanation_ko: 현재 사실과 반대되는 상황을 가정하므로 as if 뒤에 가정법 과거 were 를 쓴다. 주어가 it 이어도 was 가 아닌 were 를 쓰는 것이 원칙이다.

writing.question: 다음 조건에 맞게 우리말을 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 쇠똥구리는 어쩔 수 없이 그것을 포기하고 진짜 배설물 덩어리를 찾아 나설 수밖에 없다.
conditions: have no choice but to 를 사용할 것
abort 와 search 를 사용할 것
writing.answer: They have no choice but to abort and search for real dung balls.
writing.explanation_ko: have no choice but to+동사원형은 '~할 수밖에 없다'는 뜻이며, 뒤의 search 도 to 에 이어져 원형으로 병렬 연결된다.

writing.question: 다음 문장을 우리말로 해석하시오.
writing.en_prompt: That is why dung beetles are often spotted rolling silver arrow-reed seeds that look and smell like dung balls.
writing.answer: 그것이 바로 쇠똥구리가 배설물 덩어리처럼 보이고 냄새나는 실버 애로우리드 씨앗을 굴리는 모습이 자주 목격되는 이유이다.
writing.explanation_ko: That is why ~ 는 '그것이 ~한 이유이다'로 앞의 원인을 받고, be spotted -ing 는 '~하는 것이 목격되다'라는 수동 표현이며, that 이하는 seeds 를 수식하는 관계절이다.

writing.question: 본문의 내용에 맞게 빈칸에 알맞은 한 단어를 쓰시오.
writing.context: The seeds are dark brown and round, and their visual ___________ and smell are quite similar to antelope dung.
writing.explanation_ko: 본문에서 씨앗의 '겉모습(visual appearance)'과 냄새가 영양의 배설물과 비슷하다고 했으므로 appearance 가 알맞다.

writing.question: 본문을 한 문장으로 요약할 때 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
writing.summary: By __(A)__ dung beetles into rolling away and burying its seeds, the silver arrow-reed manages to __(B)__ and plant its seeds better.
writing.explanation_ko: 본문 마지막 문장에서 쇠똥구리를 '속임으로써(tricking)' 씨앗을 더 잘 '퍼뜨리고(spread)' 심을 수 있다고 했다.

writing.question: 다음 조건에 맞게 이 글의 주제문을 영어로 쓰시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 이 글의 주제를 한 문장으로 쓰시오.
conditions: seeds 와 dung beetles 를 반드시 포함할 것
deceive 또는 trick 을 사용할 것
writing.answer: Silver arrow-reed spreads its seeds by tricking dung beetles into burying them underground.
writing.explanation_ko: 씨앗이 배설물처럼 보여 쇠똥구리를 속이고, 그 결과 씨앗이 땅에 묻혀 퍼진다는 인과를 한 문장에 담으면 된다.
